data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction between genuine reliability gain and mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer collapses if the checklist is strictly a surface-correlational heuristic; in that regime compliance IS the mechanism, and no single evaluation can separate them because they are not distinct causal hypotheses.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is presented or treated as causally complete, so the surface-heuristic interpretation does not match the actual claim being evaluated.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The evaluation domain shifts after deployment, so the surface-correlational heuristic stops tracking the right answer and the distinction between 'was genuinely reliable' and 'was compliant on a favorable distribution' becomes retroactively meaningful.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel uses the checklist as a trigger for deeper reasoning rather than as a terminal decision rule, so compliance and genuine reliability are distinguishable even when the checklist itself is surface-level.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the checklist is explicitly a surface heuristic (correlational, non-causal), then 'following the checklist' and 'being reliable' are the same process whenever the heuristic correlates with the outcome. There is no latent structural reasoning to appeal to. Compliance that tracks the right answer is not a counterfeit of genuine reliability; it is the only kind of reliability the checklist can provide. The requested within-evaluation distinction is therefore ill-posed for surface heuristics: the distinction is real only if the checklist purports to encode causal structure.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
